verdicts.why: Nearly every sentence uses answer as a verbal reply (answered in the affirmative, answered him, made no answer), which is the first-listed gloss 'react verbally'.

senses.why: Learner line keeps both 'sufficient' and 'adequate' and both quality and quantity; example 'A few kind words will answer' uses the sense; null is fine.
Learner line covers 'satisfactory for', 'meet the requirements' and 'serve the purpose'; example 'will answer our needs' fits; null is fine.
Learner line renders 'liable or accountable' as responsible / must explain and face consequences; 'answer for what he has done' fits; describes without judging.
Learner line keeps both 'defence' and 'refutation' of a charge or argument; example 'answered the charges against her' uses the sense; null is fine.
'Match or correspond' is rendered as match / be in agreement with; 'answered to the description of the thief' is the same sense; null is fine.
Learner line covers both stimulus and command; 'The horse answered the rein' is a react-to-stimulus use; null is fine.

The example's answer takes a question ('what his last words had meant') as its object, which reads as resolving or giving the answer to a question (the neighbouring 'give the correct answer or solution to' sense) rather than plainly 'understand the meaning of'; a learner would be taught 'answer = understand' from a sentence that shows answering a question. The learner line itself is faithful, and this is a borderline call.
